intents.description: Greets the patient and introduces self or role.
intents.example: Hello, I'm Dr. ___, one of the doctors here.

intents.description: Explains confidentiality and its limits.
intents.example: What you tell me stays between us and the care team, unless I'm worried about your safety.

intents.description: Asks an open question that invites the patient to talk freely.
intents.example: Tell me more about what's been happening.

intents.description: Asks what brought the patient in or what the main problem is.
intents.example: What brings you in today?

intents.description: Asks when the problem started, how long it has lasted or how it has changed.
intents.example: When did this start, and what was going on at the time?

intents.description: Asks how the patient's mood or feelings have been.
intents.example: How has your mood been these last few weeks?

intents.description: Asks about sleep.
intents.example: How have you been sleeping?

intents.description: Asks about appetite, eating or weight.
intents.example: How is your appetite, and has your weight changed?

intents.description: Asks about energy or tiredness.
intents.example: How is your energy through the day?

intents.description: Asks about concentration, memory or focus.
intents.example: How is your concentration, at work or reading?

intents.description: Asks about loss of interest or enjoyment in usual activities.
intents.example: Are there things you used to enjoy that you've stopped doing?

intents.description: Asks about thoughts of death, not wanting to live, self-harm or suicide.
intents.example: Sometimes when people feel this low they have thoughts of not wanting to be alive. Have you had thoughts like that?

intents.description: Asks about a suicide plan, intent, preparations or past attempts.
intents.example: Have you thought about how you might end your life, or made any plans?

intents.description: Asks about access to means (tablets, pesticides, weapons and so on).
intents.example: Do you have anything at home you might use, like tablets or poison?

intents.description: Asks what keeps the patient going, reasons for living, or supports.
intents.example: What keeps you going on the hard days?

intents.description: Asks about thoughts of harming others.
intents.example: Have you had any thoughts of harming anyone else?

intents.description: Asks about hearing voices or seeing things others do not.
intents.example: Have you heard or seen things that other people don't?

intents.description: Asks about unusual beliefs, being watched, followed or controlled.
intents.example: Have you felt that people are watching you or trying to harm you?

intents.description: Asks about alcohol: whether, what, how much or how often they drink, drinking in the morning, or losing control of it.
intents.example: Tell me about your drinking: what do you have, and how much on a usual day?

intents.description: Asks about drugs, tobacco, cannabis, pills or other substances other than alcohol.
intents.example: Do you smoke or use any other drugs or pills?

intents.description: Asks when they last drank or used (the last drink, last night, this morning).
intents.example: When did you last have a drink?

intents.description: Asks what happens when they stop or cut down: shakes, sweats, fits or seizures, seeing things, confusion; or about past attempts to stop.
intents.example: Has anything happened when you stopped suddenly, like shakes, a fit or seeing things?

intents.description: Asks about past mental health problems, treatment, or periods of elevated mood.
intents.example: Have you ever seen a psychiatrist or had treatment for your mental health?

intents.description: Asks about current or past medicines.
intents.example: Are you taking any medicines at the moment?

intents.description: Asks about allergies.
intents.example: Are you allergic to any medicines?

intents.description: Asks about physical illnesses or medical history.
intents.example: Do you have any medical problems?

intents.description: Asks about illness, including mental illness, in the family.
intents.example: Has anyone in your family had problems with their mental health or with drinking?

intents.description: Asks about work, living situation, relationships, finances or family set-up.
intents.example: How are things at work and at home?

intents.description: Asks about abuse or traumatic experiences.
intents.example: Has anything very difficult or frightening happened to you?

intents.description: Asks about pregnancy, periods or contraception.
intents.example: Is there any chance you could be pregnant?

intents.description: Acknowledges or validates the patient's feelings.
intents.example: That sounds really hard. It makes sense you feel worn out.

intents.description: Summarises what the patient has said.
intents.example: Let me check I've understood: ...

intents.description: Checks the patient understood, or checks own understanding.
intents.example: Does that make sense? What questions do you have?

intents.description: Explains the patient's legal status on the ward and their rights honestly (for example that an independent patient may ask to leave, and what happens next).
intents.example: You're here voluntarily, which means ...

intents.description: Checks whether the patient understands the decision, its likely consequences, and can communicate a choice.
intents.example: Can you tell me in your own words what we've talked about and what might happen?

intents.description: Offers the patient real options or asks what would help, instead of telling them what to do.
intents.example: We have a couple of options; what would suit you?

intents.description: Asks why the patient wants something (for example to leave) and what worries them about staying.
intents.example: What would going home give you that you're missing here?

intents.description: Threatens, orders or pressures the patient (for example 'you can't leave', 'we'll lock you up', 'calm down or else').
Judging, blaming, dismissive, mocking or abusive language.
Cuts the patient off or talks over them.
